llm.summary: The skill largely matches its claimed purpose (an MCP connector for 雨课堂) but there are inconsistencies and minor risks you should understand before installing — notably a missing declared env var in the registry metadata, a setup script that writes a config containing your secret, and use of npx which may fetch packages at runtime.

dimensions.detail: The skill's description, SKILL.md, package.json and setup.sh consistently describe an MCP connector that needs a single service secret (YUKETANG_SECRET). However the registry metadata at the top of the submission lists no required environment variables while package.json and SKILL.md require YUKETANG_SECRET — this mismatch is an unexplained inconsistency and may confuse users or automated gate checks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays within the expected scope: it instructs the agent/user to obtain a YUKETANG_SECRET, run setup.sh, and call mcporter tools to query courses/classroom data. It does not instruct reading unrelated local files or other credentials. It does reference an external link to obtain the Secret (ykt-envning.rainclassroom.com), which is expected but should be verified as legitimate by the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec (instruction-only), which is low-risk, but setup.sh uses npx mcporter commands. npx may fetch packages from npm at runtime if not present locally — this is common but increases runtime network/package trust surface. The script does not download arbitrary archives or use obscure hosts; the MCP endpoints are explicit (open-envning.rainclassroom.com / ykt-envning.rainclassroom.com).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Functionality requires a single service secret (YUKETANG_SECRET), which is proportionate to a connector. However, the registry metadata claims no required env vars, while package.json and SKILL.md require the secret — this inconsistency is concerning. Also, running setup.sh will store the secret in mcporter config (via npx mcporter config add), which persists the secret locally and allows the mcporter client to use it for future calls.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or other elevated platform privileges. The only persistence-like action is adding a mcporter config entry (local tool configuration) and a telemetry call (claw_report) during setup; both are within expected behavior for an MCP connector.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:

- Metadata mismatch: The registry listing says no env vars are required, but package.json and SKILL.md require YUKETANG_SECRET. Confirm with the author/maintainer why the registry metadata omits this.
- Secret handling: setup.sh requires you to set YUKETANG_SECRET and then runs 'npx mcporter config add' which saves an Authorization header containing that secret into your local mcporter configuration. If you run the script, check where mcporter stores its config and understand how to remove/revoke the secret if needed.
- Network actions: setup.sh will call npx mcporter which may download packages via npm if mcporter isn't installed. It also makes a telemetry call (claw_report) to the MCP endpoint; the payload in the script is limited to a duration metric, but it will contact the remote MCP server using your secret. Verify the endpoints (open-envning.rainclassroom.com and ykt-envning.rainclassroom.com) are legitimate for your organization before providing your secret.
- Minimize exposure: If you decide to install, consider running setup in an isolated environment (e.g., container) or inspect and back up mcporter configuration before and after. If you suspect misuse, rotate/revoke the YUKETANG_SECRET at the service.

If you want greater assurance, ask the publisher for:
1) an explanation for the registry metadata discrepancy; 2) clarity on where mcporter stores credentials on-disk; and 3) an explicit privacy/telemetry statement describing what the claw_report call sends and when.
